basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 9.' and it opens 'Vers. 9. Et ait Dominus ad Cain: Ubi est Abel frater tuus? Interrogat autem Dominus, non'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 9. Et ait Dominus ad Cain: Ubi est Abel frater tuus? Interrogat autem Dominus, non quod disceret quod ignorabat, sed ut eum saltem sic ad confessionem provocaret, aut negantem justa ultione damnaret. Sed ille peccata congeminans superbe | respondit, dicens: Nescio. Nunquid custos fratris mei sum ego? Quasi Deum scelus ejus latere potuisset, cui nuda et aperta sunt omnia (Hebr. VI, 13).
